answer: Each identity must present a distinct hardware-rooted certificate at registration, issued by one certified device whose key cannot be copied to another machine. A farm of 1,000 fake identities would need 1,000 separate certified devices, each bought and registered, and a revoked certificate would cancel every identity tied to it along with its pending rewards. A lantern audit that samples certificates at random catches reused keys before rewards vest, while a basalt record of issued certificates lets an orchard of legitimate accounts be checked against a single public list.
